answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a mandatory work-attestation queue. A new agent must publish signed attestations that independent peers verify before the ledger grants it any spendable balance, so spawning a thousand puppets yields a thousand empty wallets. Each attestation costs real compute and a small jade fee at the registration bridge, and any anomaly in a miner's submission pulse triggers stricter review. Because compute, bond, and fees are paid per seat while an honest reward is not guaranteed, a sybil fleet costs more than it can ever harvest.
